The AB17 v1-versus-2024 size comparison reproduces exactly, the six specs validate and fit the PM-01 envelope, superseding AB14 is sound, and no José decision is needed. The scripts are close: exclusivity, the size allowance, ZIP-prefix handling, CRC coverage, STOP and memory polling (which works under a 256 MiB address-space limit) and the CRC classifier all behave correctly under adversarial synthetic fixtures. evidence: I ran a scratchpad probe calling acquire() with fake lister and opener, a 52-file GT21-layout listing, and stored ZIPs.

Pass: a prefixed or unprefixed ZIP is acquired_verified_not_extracted. A changed listing ts is refused before the output root is created. An extra member, Content-Length below the listing, a short body, a wrong Content-Disposition, a traversal or mixed-prefix member, short disk and short memory are all refused. A STOP file mid-stream is refused with the .partial preserved. An existing output root is refused with nothing written. A receipt directory inside the output root is refused.

Exclusivity: the receipt dir is created with mkdir(exist_ok=False), every receipt with open('x'), the output root with mkdir(exist_ok=False), and publication uses os.link, which does not clobber. _inside resolves symlinked parents. The CLI cannot skip the re-list (the lister is a function parameter only).

Size allowance (1 KiB per file + 64 KiB): safe. The observed AB12 overhead is 362,042 B for 1,770 files (about 205 B per file), inside the 1,876,544 B allowance. Any compression makes Content-Length < listed bytes and is refused (fail closed). The audit text says '≤ 1 MiB above the listing sum' and 'differing from the HEAD-time value'; the script uses the per-file rule and no HEAD. That is acceptable, but the audit text should match.
ZIP-prefix ambiguity: handled. It is all-prefixed or all-unprefixed, mixed is refused, and any other wrapper name fails path equality.
CRC coverage: every non-directory member is streamed. Byte count and CRC32 are recomputed against the central directory, zipfile also checks the CRC at EOF, and the SHA-256 per member is recorded.

STOP and memory: guard() runs before every 1 MiB read and before every member. Windows memory is polled at most every 15 s. I ran windows_free_mib() and an HTTPS request in a process with RLIMIT_AS 256 MiB; both work (6,372 MiB free reported, HTTP 200).

FAILED, ordering: the archive is linked to <out>/<subject>.zip and the .partial removed before check_zip and hash_members. In the 'extra member' probe, the refused archive remains as AB99.zip with status failed_preserved. The launcher's expected_output_names ['AB17.zip'] would also see a rejected archive under the accepted name.

FAILED, live copy: a same-size content change in the ZIP is accepted ('same-size content change' probe → acquired_verified_not_extracted). The listing is checked only before the download. The 2024 folder is demonstrably live (AB28 opensim.log dated 2026-10-11), and a change during the download would show in the Dropbox ts but not in ZIP sizes.
